articles.title: Casa onde Lula viveu na infância segue de pé em Guarujá após 70 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente morou no distrito de Vicente de Carvalho por quase quatro anos, depois de deixar o Agreste de Pernambuco em uma viagem de caminhão pau de arara com a mãe e os irmãos.
articles.summary: Presidente morou no distrito de Vicente de Carvalho por quase quatro anos, depois de deixar o Agreste de Pernambuco em uma viagem de caminhão pau de arara com a mãe e os irmãos.
articles.body:
Casa onde o presidente da República, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, viveu na infância segue de pé em Guarujá, SP. — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert e Marcos Romor

A casa onde Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) viveu parte da infância em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo, permanece de pé mais de sete décadas depois da chegada da família à região. Apesar das transformações pelas quais o bairro passou ao longo dos anos, o imóvel ainda conserva elementos da construção original e mantém viva uma parte da história do presidente da República.

A propriedade, localizada na antiga região de Itapema, atual Vicente de Carvalho, pertence à família de Marcos Romor desde a década de 1980, quando foi adquirida pelos avós dele. Atualmente, o imóvel conta com três quartos, além de sala, cozinha e banheiro.

Ao g1 , Marcos contou que, após a morte dos avós, comprou a casa dos tios e realizou uma reforma, preservando parte da estrutura. Atualmente, a mãe dele mora no local.

“A casa permanece com a mesma estrutura e tem aproximadamente 100 anos. Meus avós compraram, eles eram amigos do ex-proprietário. Quando os meus avós faleceram, comprei dos meus tios e reformei deixando a parte do chalé intacta, devido aos laços de família”, relatou.

Mais de 70 anos depois da chegada dos Silva ao litoral paulista, a construção ainda guarda elementos de sua estrutura original, incluindo uma parede de madeira e os fundos da residência.

Veja detalhes que permanecem preservados desde a época em que Lula morou no imóvel

Antes de se tornar o primeiro presidente da história do Brasil a ser eleito quatro vezes pelo voto popular, Lula viveu parte da infância em Guarujá. Aos sete anos, deixou o Agreste de Pernambuco com a mãe e os irmãos em uma viagem de mais de 2 mil quilômetros, feita em um caminhão pau de arara.

Em 1945, os pais de Lula, Aristides Inácio da Silva e Eurídice Ferreira de Mello, conhecida como Dona Lindu, moravam no sítio Vargem Comprida, em Caetés, no Agreste pernambucano. A região enfrentava um período de seca, que comprometia as lavouras e dificultava o acesso da família a alimentos e água.

Aristides Inácio da Silva e Dona Lindu, os pais de Lula — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Lula

Com a mulher grávida de oito meses e os seis filhos, Aristides decidiu deixar o Nordeste e seguir para São Paulo em busca de trabalho. Ele se estabeleceu no litoral paulista e conseguiu emprego como carregador de sacas de café em um armazém de Santos.

Durante esse período, levou consigo, escondida de Dona Lindu, Mocinha, prima de sua mulher, então com 15 anos e grávida dele. Os dois passaram a morar em uma casa de madeira no distrito de Vicente de Carvalho, em Guarujá.

Em 1950, Aristides voltou a Pernambuco e reencontrou os filhos. Depois, retornou ao litoral paulista acompanhado de Jaime, irmão de Lula. Dois anos mais tarde, Dona Lindu decidiu reunir as crianças, vender a casa e os poucos pertences que possuíam e partir ao encontro do marido.

Primeira foto de Lula, aos 3 anos, ao lado da irmã Maria Baixinha. — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Lula

Em dezembro de 1952, aos sete anos, Lula embarcou com a mãe e os irmãos em um caminhão pau de arara. A viagem até o litoral paulista durou 13 dias e 13 noites. Ao longo dos cerca de 2,5 mil quilômetros, a família enfrentou dificuldades para descansar e precisou improvisar abrigos durante o percurso.

Depois de chegar ao bairro do Brás, na capital paulista, os retirantes seguiram de táxi e, posteriormente, de balsa até Guarujá. Foi no distrito de Itapema, atual Vicente de Carvalho, que reencontraram Aristides e começaram uma nova etapa da vida.

Dona Lindu e os filhos passaram a morar em uma casa de madeira na região, que não contava com serviços básicos, como água encanada e energia elétrica. A jornalista e escritora Denise Paraná descreveu as condições da residência no livro Lula, o filho do Brasil.

“E assim Lindu, Lula e seus irmãos passaram a morar numa velha casinha de madeira em Vicente de Carvalho, sem água encanada, poço próximo ou luz elétrica, mas muito além daquilo que imaginavam ter um dia na vida”.

A chegada ao litoral não significou o fim das dificuldades. Aristides havia formado outra família durante o período em que viveu longe de Dona Lindu e dos filhos. Para ajudar nas despesas, a mãe de Lula recolhia grãos de café que caíam nas calçadas dos armazéns do Porto de Santos e os vendia .

Dona Lindu, Lula e seus irmãos — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Lula

Lula também começou a trabalhar ainda criança para contribuir com a renda familiar. Ao lado do irmão Frei Chico, três anos mais velho, vendia amendoim, tapioca e laranjas no cais de Santos. Mais tarde, passou a trabalhar como engraxate no Centro da cidade.

Foi em Guarujá que Lula iniciou a vida escolar. Em 1954, passou a frequentar a Escola Estadual Marcílio Dias, em Vicente de Carvalho, onde estudou até a mudança para São Paulo, em 1956.

Ele frequentava as aulas sem que o pai soubesse. Aristides era contrário aos estudos e havia proibido os filhos de estudar e brincar.

A convivência familiar foi marcada por conflitos. Em 1955, Dona Lindu decidiu se separar de Aristides. No ano seguinte, mudou-se com os filhos para a capital paulista . A família passou a morar na Vila Carioca, bairro operário no distrito do Ipiranga, em um pequeno cômodo nos fundos de um bar arrendado por um tio.

Escola Estadual Marcilio Dias, onde Lula estudou, em Guarujá — Foto: Google Steet View

A passagem da família pelo litoral paulista também está relacionada a uma particularidade da história de Lula: a divergência entre sua data de nascimento e o registro civil. Embora o presidente comemore o aniversário em 27 de outubro, seus documentos indicam o dia 6 do mesmo mês.

A diferença está relacionada às dificuldades enfrentadas pela família para registrar os filhos. Na época, a distância dos cartórios e as condições de vida no interior de Pernambuco dificultavam a emissão dos documentos logo após os nascimentos. Os registros de Lula e dos irmãos foram providenciados posteriormente, já em Santos.

Em relato sobre o episódio, Frei Chico contou que Dona Lindu levou ao cartório uma lista com os nomes e as datas de nascimento dos filhos, mas acabou se confundindo durante o atendimento.

“Minha mãe foi ao cartório em Santos registrar os filhos. Levou anotado todos as datas e os nomes. Mas acredito que ficou intimidada pela atitude da escrivã, que sugeriu mudar o nome da minha irmã, ali, na hora de Sebastiana para a Ruth, seu próprio nome em sua ‘homenagem’, e ela acabou se atrapalhando com tantas datas”, contou o irmão.

Lula comemorando seu aniversário de 81 anos — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

Aristides trabalhou por mais de duas décadas no Porto de Santos como ensacador de café, carregando sacas durante a movimentação de mercadorias no cais.

Nos últimos anos de vida, enfrentou problemas relacionados ao alcoolismo e morreu em 1978, em Vicente de Carvalho. Segundo informações do Instituto Lula, ele foi sepultado como indigente.

Décadas depois de deixar Guarujá ainda criança, Lula voltou ao município em diferentes ocasiões, já como presidente da República . Entre os destinos estava o Forte dos Andradas , instalação militar que conta com estrutura de hospedagem e acesso restrito.

O complexo abriga a Praia do Monduba, uma faixa de areia de aproximadamente 400 metros cercada pela Mata Atlântica e cujo acesso é controlado pelo Exército.

As visitas ocorreram em diferentes momentos dos mandatos presidenciais e também depois que Lula deixou o cargo:

Abril de 2006: estadia para descanso no complexo militar.

Janeiro de 2007 : período de férias após a posse para o segundo mandato.

Fevereiro de 2008 : viagem durante o feriado de Carnaval.

Janeiro de 2010 : período de descanso antes do retorno aos compromissos em Brasília.

Janeiro de 2011 : já fora da Presidência, Lula passou cerca de 12 dias no Forte com filhos e netos, a convite do Ministério da Defesa e do Exército.

Presidente e governador de SP lançaram o edital do Túnel Santos-Guarujá nesta quinta-feira (27) — Foto: Vanessa Rodrigues/AT

articles.title: Wage unrest grips Bangladesh garment sector; dozens of factories shut
articles.summary: Bangladesh will constitute a wage board on Sunday to review salaries in its garment industry after protests over pay shortages disrupted factory
articles.body: Bangladesh will constitute a wage board on Sunday to review salaries in its garment industry after protests over pay shortages disrupted factory operations, shut dozens of manufacturing units and led to clashes between workers and police.Garment workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of 30,000 taka ($245), more than double the existing minimum of 12,500 taka. They say rising expenses on food, housing, transport and healthcare have significantly reduced their purchasing power.Labour and employment minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the government would formally set up the wage board following discussions with labour leaders and industry representatives in an effort to resolve the unrest, Reuters reported.The protests intensified on Saturday, with around 30 garment factories in Ashulia, a major manufacturing hub on the outskirts of Dhaka, declaring holidays, according to Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of the Ashulia Industrial Police.Hundreds of workers also blocked a major intersection in Dhaka, while demonstrations in other industrial areas disrupted traffic and factory operations. Clashes between protesters and police in Ashulia left several people injured, including police personnel. Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse the demonstrators.Chowdhury appealed to workers to return to their jobs, saying the decision to review the wage structure addressed their primary demand. He warned that continued factory closures and production disruptions could delay export consignments and payments from international buyers, adding to the financial pressure on manufacturers and workers.Wage dispute puts key export industry under pressureThe unrest has raised concerns over Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) sector, which employs around four million people and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings.The industry, the world's second-largest garment exporter after China, contributes around 10% to Bangladesh's gross domestic product and remains a major pillar of its economy. It also supplies clothing to several leading international and Western brands.Manufacturers, however, have flagged mounting operational challenges, including higher production costs, recurring shortages of gas and electricity, and uncertainty in energy markets amid tensions in the Middle East.The wage dispute comes at a difficult time for the sector, with prolonged industrial disruptions threatening production schedules and the timely fulfilment of overseas orders.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2021, an Ohio couple signed a deal to share house-sale proceeds if they split; after their breakup and a $71,897 dispute, judges upheld the agreement, giving the woman $41,466 despite a fight over renovation spending
articles.summary: A man in Ohio who refused to share money from the sale of his house with his former partner has lost a court battle over an agreement they signed when
articles.body: A man in Ohio who refused to share money from the sale of his house with his former partner has lost a court battle over an agreement they signed when they were planning to get married. James R Cline argued that his former partner, Ashley A Lokash, had not spent enough money on improving the house to claim a share of the sale proceeds. However, on October 26, an Ohio appeals court ruled in Lokash's favour, allowing her to receive $41,466.50 from the sale.The dispute began with a house the couple bought in Niles, Ohio, in 2021, according to Mortgage Professional America (MPA). At the time, they planned a future together and decided to invest in the property. Although the house was registered only in Cline's name, Lokash agreed to contribute money towards renovations and other improvements. They financed the purchase through a loan guaranteed by the US Department of Veterans Affairs.In September 2021, they signed a written agreement explaining how their money would be handled. Lokash could spend up to $40,000 on improving the property. If the house was later sold, she would first receive reimbursement for her spending, up to the agreed limit. The money remaining after that would be divided equally between them.But their plans changed within months. The relationship ended in March 2022, and Lokash moved out of the house. Cline continued living there and kept furniture that she had purchased. Although they were no longer together, the agreement they had signed remained in place. That became a problem when Cline decided to sell the property.House sale turned into court battleIn September 2022, around six months after their separation, Cline put the house up for sale. Lokash wanted to ensure that the money she had contributed would be taken into account when the property was sold.She submitted a copy of their agreement and a written statement to the local property records office so anyone checking the property's records could see that she was claiming a share of the money from its sale. When Premiere Settlement & Title, the company handling the sale, examined the records, it discovered her claim.The house was sold to a buyer in December 2023, but the disagreement continued. The company paid Cline $15,000 and kept another $55,568.51 aside because it could not decide who should receive it.Rather than release the money to either person, the company asked the court to settle the matter. The total amount involved in the dispute was $71,897.61.Man refused to share the moneyCline believed Lokash had not done enough to receive the money promised under their agreement. His argument was that she had agreed to spend money improving the house but had contributed only a small amount compared with the $40,000 mentioned in the document. He therefore argued that the agreement should not be enforced because she had not fulfilled her part of the arrangement.However, the judges found that Cline had misunderstood an important part of what the couple had signed. The agreement did not say Lokash must spend $40,000. It only set that amount as the maximum she could contribute. This meant she could spend less and still meet the conditions of their arrangement.The court examined records showing that Lokash had spent $1,191.34 on materials after the agreement was signed. Her purchases included paint and supplies from Sherwin Williams, items from Handyman and carpeting from Tondo Carpets.Cline also questioned whether these purchases had actually improved the property. But the judges found another problem with his argument. The materials Lokash had bought were in Cline's possession, and he had chosen not to use them. The court concluded that he could not use his own decision not to use the materials as a reason to deny her the money promised under the agreement.How much money did the woman receive?After examining the agreement and the couple's spending records, the court upheld the earlier decision in Lokash's favour. The judges found that she had contributed money towards the property and that the agreement did not require her to spend the full $40,000.Lokash was entitled to $11,035.38 as reimbursement for earlier expenses. This included $2,525 she had contributed towards buying the house and $3,325 spent on flooring and carpeting. The remaining amount covered other purchases, including hardware and furnishings.She was also entitled to half of the net proceeds from the house sale, amounting to $30,431.12. Together, these payments brought her total share to $41,466.50.Cline was entitled to the remaining money, including the $15,000 that the company had already paid him.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'India not a banana republic': BJP attacks Rahul Gandhi ahead of INDIA bloc rally
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union minister JP Nadda on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the Congress and Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, accusing the opposition of using the banner of democracy to create unrest, damage the economy and destabilise an elected government.Reacting to the 'Chalo Delhi' mobilisation, Nadda said the rally was a “calculated conspiracy to plunge the nation into anarchy—in the name of democracy”. He described it as a “foolish, orchestrated drama” by parties that had been defeated and rejected by voters.Nadda further said that it will prove to be the final "nail in the coffin" of Congress' "political downfall".Addressing Rahul Gandhi directly, the Union minister outlined what he called the Congress leader's model of politics, alleging that it involved spreading misinformation, provoking street protests, harming the economy and seeking to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers.“The first stage is spreading lies and rumours; the second is inciting anarchy and chaos on the streets; the third is damaging the nation’s economy; and the fourth is attempting to destabilise an elected government at the behest of foreign powers,” Nadda said.He also alleged that the November 1 rally had four specific objectives: hurting the sentiments of the Sikh community, triggering violence in Delhi to bring down a democratically elected government, affecting the earnings of traders during the festive season and damaging India's reputation.Nadda's remarks came amid the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls and its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."Rahul Gandhi, listen carefully: this is India—not some 'banana republic' where you can incite arson, trigger riots, or push an agenda for 'regime change' whenever you please. Stop dreaming, Rahul Gandhi. India is the world’s oldest and most robust democracy. November 1st stands as the most infamous and darkest stain in India’s democratic history. On this very day, goons nurtured by the Congress party massacred our innocent Sikh brethren. Thousands of Sikh families were rendered homeless overnight, and thousands of women were widowed. The nation has not forgotten; even today, the 'Widow Colony' in Delhi bears witness to that horrific and bloody chapter of Congress history. To this day, the Gandhi family has not offered a sincere apology to the Sikh community for that grave sin. Observe the insensitivity of the Congress and the petty mindset of Rahul Gandhi. On this dark day—a day when the nation ought to be remembering its martyrs and victims—Rahul Gandhi stands at Ramlila Maidan, seeking only to further his own political agenda ...", Nadda added.BJP accuses Opposition of disrupting peace and businessThe rally has also drawn criticism from the BJP over its timing, with the ruling party accusing Congress of holding a political event on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.BJP is holding a separate march in West Delhi under the banner of remembering the victims of the 1984 violence.The march is scheduled to proceed from Hari Nagar Bus Depot to Tilak Nagar Metro Station, with Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta, Delhi BJP president and other party leaders expected to participate.Meanwhile, the BJP and its Mahayuti allies held a 'Lokshahi Bachao, Anarajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy) padyatra in Mumbai on Sunday.Maharashtra BJP president Ravindra Chavan accused the Congress of spreading what he described as false narratives about constitutional institutions, including the judiciary and Parliament.“At a time when the entire nation is witnessing a phase of development-oriented governance under the leadership of PM Modi, the opposition Congress party is, without any valid reason, attempting to create confusion among the public by propagating false narratives about our established institutions,” Chavan said.Shiv Sena MP Naresh Mhaske also criticised Rahul Gandhi and his associates, alleging that their activities were against the Constitution.BJP has also launched a nationwide 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' campaign to counter opposition allegations relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Party workers are expected to reach villages and households to present the BJP's position on the electoral process.INDIA bloc leaders allege voter irregularities, restrictions on rally supportersThe opposition alliance, meanwhile, has maintained that its mobilisation is aimed at protecting democratic rights and raising concerns over alleged deletions of legitimate voters from electoral rolls.Himachal Pradesh deputy chief minister Mukesh Agnihotri alleged that buses carrying supporters from his state were being stopped at different points on their way to Delhi.He claimed that some vehicles were intercepted over pollution norms and others over taxation issues, despite the buses being BS-VI-compliant.“We had already instructed everyone that such obstructions might occur, and if stopped, they should simply continue on foot to reach Himachal Bhawan,” Agnihotri said, adding that the supporters were prepared to walk to Ramlila Maidan.Himachal Pradesh minister Vikramaditya Singh called for accountability from Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and claimed that the number of votes involved in the alleged irregularities had risen from 13 crore to around 16 crore.“I am confident that, in the near future, the CEC Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign, and a new revolution will sweep across the entire country,” Singh said.Uttarakhand leader of opposition Yashpal Arya described the rally as a “battle for justice” to protect democracy and the Constitution. Congress leader Kunwar Danish Ali also called the mobilisation historic and accused the government of targeting students, young people and farmers.The INDIA bloc has demanded the replacement of electronic voting machines with paper ballots and the immediate resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people in Delhi and neighbouring states to join the march, either from Connaught Place or directly at Ramlila Maidan.Heavy security arrangements across DelhiSecurity has been tightened across the national capital in view of the two political events. Nearly 10,000 police and paramilitary personnel, including Delhi Police, Central Armed Police Forces, the CRPF and Rapid Action Force, have been deployed across Central and New Delhi, ANI reported.More than 4,000 personnel have been stationed around Ramlila Maidan, along the route from Minto Bridge and in surrounding areas. Barricades have also been placed around Connaught Place, Jantar Mantar, Bhagwan Das Road and areas near the Supreme Court and the Election Commission's office.Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita has been imposed in sensitive areas to prevent large unauthorised gatherings. Security agencies are also using CCTV cameras, AI-enabled facial recognition systems and drones to monitor crowd movement.At the Delhi-Gurugram border, Border Security Force personnel have been deployed alongside police units to monitor entry points into the capital. Authorities have installed barricades on major routes connecting the two cities and are checking suspicious vehicles.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Every single shop forcibly shut': Rahul Gandhi targets BJP over Connaught Place closures during mega rally
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of causing financial losses to local traders by allegedly
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of causing financial losses to local traders by allegedly forcing shops in Delhi's Connaught Place to shut on the day of the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Delhi' march and mega rally at Ramlila Maidan. The Leader of the Opposition claimed that the closures hurt businesses despite his appeal to rally participants to support local traders by shopping in the capital.In a post on X on Sunday, Rahul said participants travelling to the national capital had been encouraged to shop at local markets during their visit. However, he claimed that they found shops closed upon reaching Connaught Place."We told everyone that when you come here for the march and the mega rally, buy things, do some shopping. But, while coming to Connaught Place here, we found out that the BJP has forcibly shut down every single shop. So, you should know who is causing the loss to the traders, and how it's happening!" Rahul said.The remarks followed an appeal Rahul had made in a video message on X late on Saturday, urging people arriving in Delhi from different parts of the country to support small businesses during the festive season."Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here," he said."Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders," Rahul added.The Congress leader also rejected concerns that the gathering would hurt businesses, accusing the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's economic impact."I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours," he said, reiterating his appeal for participants to purchase goods from local shops.The appeal came amid objections from traders' associations, which had urged Rahul and Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi to postpone the November 1 demonstration until after the festive season.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) warned that an estimated 10 lakh participants and 15,000-20,000 vehicles could cause severe congestion across central Delhi."We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown," the traders' body said.The Federation of Sadar Bazar Traders Association also flagged the potential impact on festive business, estimating that the period from Dhanteras to Diwali accounts for around Rs 25,000 crore in turnover. It sought postponement of the rally until after November 10.Meanwhile, thousands of supporters and senior opposition leaders gathered in the national capital on Sunday for the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Delhi' protest march and mega rally at Ramlila Maidan, prompting heightened security arrangements and traffic restrictions across parts of central Delhi.Several prominent leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, AICC General Secretary KC Venugopal, West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, Trinamool Congress General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy and RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav, joined the procession after departing from the Constitution Club.Carrying banners reading 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao', the opposition leaders are protesting alleged electoral roll irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The INDIA bloc has also demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged large-scale voter omissions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Punjab polls: In a blow to AAP, 2 MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, quit party after 1st candidate list announcement
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: Two AAP MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour, both in Punjab's Patiala district have resigned
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: Two AAP MLAs, Chetan Singh Jouramajra from Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra from Sanour, both in Punjab's Patiala district have resigned from the party's primary membership on Sunday, a day after the Aam Aadmi Party released its first list of 40 candidates for the 2027 assembly elections.The party, however, has not yet announced its candidates for either constituency.According to news agency PTI, Pathanmajra sent his resignation letter to AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal, Jouramajra, a former Punjab minister, announced his decision in a social media post.The resignations come as AAP begins preparations for the 2027 polls.In September, the party appointed former Punjab minister Surjit Singh Rakhra as its halqa (constituency) in-charge for Samana. Rakhra is being seen as a possible candidate from the seat, although the party has not officially declared him as its nominee.Pathanmajra, meanwhile, has previously questioned the functioning of the AAP government in Punjab.He has also been facing a rape case registered in September last year following a complaint by a woman from Zirakpur. She alleged that Pathanmajra had misrepresented himself as a divorcee, entered into a relationship with her and married her in 2021 despite already being married.The Punjab Police arrested Pathanmajra in Madhya Pradesh's Gwalior in March this year, more than six months after he allegedly escaped police custody in connection with the case.In May, the Punjab and Haryana high court granted him regular bail in the case.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.summary: Violent protests have erupted in Bangladesh's garment industry as workers demand a sharp increase in their minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka to 30,000
articles.body: Violent protests have erupted in Bangladesh's garment industry as workers demand a sharp increase in their minimum monthly wage from 12,500 taka to 30,000 taka. Clashes, vandalism and road blockades have been reported in Dhaka and Gazipur, prompting authorities to deploy police and Border Guard Bangladesh personnel to restore order.The unrest, which began on Saturday, escalated on Sunday in industrial areas such as Mirpur in Dhaka and Konabari in Gazipur. Protesters allegedly vandalised factories, attacked police outposts with stones and set police vehicles on fire. Several major roads were blocked using barricades, disrupting movement.Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse crowds as demonstrations intensified. Border Guard Bangladesh units were also deployed alongside police to maintain security in the affected areas.What's the demandGarment workers are demanding a monthly minimum wage of 30,000 taka, more than twice the existing minimum of 12,500 taka. Their demand comes amid a recent government announcement of a new pay scale for public sector employees, which is expected to nearly double their salaries and benefits.Workers are seeking a comparable improvement in their earnings, arguing for a substantial increase in wages. However, factory owners say they are struggling with declining orders, stagnant product prices and rising costs of imported raw materials. They have argued that meeting the workers' demand would be difficult under current conditions.Wage board formed, but protests continueThe Bangladesh government has formed a wage board to decide on a revised minimum wage for garment workers. However, the move has not brought the demonstrations to an end, with workers continuing to protest for higher pay.The dispute has put the spotlight on Bangladesh's ready-made garment (RMG) industry, which grew rapidly from the late 1970s and early 1980s to become the backbone of the country's export economy.The sector accounts for more than 80 per cent of Bangladesh's export earnings and employs around four million people. Women make up an estimated 60 to 70 per cent of its workforce, making the industry a major source of employment and economic opportunity for them.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: US midterms 2026: Early voting surpasses 50.5 million, Texas sees significant voter turnout increase
articles.summary: Early voting for the 2026 US midterms has eclipsed 50.5 million, marking a notable increase from 2022. Texas experiences a significant rise in voter turnout, especially in Harris County, intensifying the competitive landscape as both parties vie for control of Congress during President Trump's second term.
articles.body: More than 50.5 million Americans have voted early ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections, nearly five million more than the total recorded during the 2022 midterms. The increase comes as both parties face closely contested races that could determine control of Congress for the final two years of President Donald Trump's second term.Data from the University of Florida's Election Lab showed that early voting had surpassed 50.5 million by Saturday morning, ahead of Tuesday's election.Among states that track voters' party affiliations, registered Democrats accounted for 10.7 million early ballots, compared with 7.8 million from registered Republicans. These figures reflect the political registration of voters who have cast ballots and do not indicate which candidates they have supported.The higher number of Democratic voters comes as Republicans face competitive contests in states that have traditionally favoured the party. Dissatisfaction with Trump's presidency and concerns about the cost of living have also become prominent issues in the campaign.Republicans currently hold a 53-47 majority in the Senate and are seeking to retain control of the chamber. Democrats are targeting traditionally Republican-leaning states, including Texas, Alaska and Kansas, where competitive races could help them secure a majority.Texas has become a major focus of the contest, with more than seven million people having already voted early, as per the University data. This is around 1.5 million more than the number recorded in the state during the 2022 midterms.The increase is also evident in Harris County, which includes Houston. By Wednesday, 862,700 people had cast early ballots there, compared with 564,500 at the same point in the 2022 election, the Associated Press analysis has found.Harris County has consistently backed Democratic candidates in recent elections. In 2024, Kamala Harris defeated Trump in the county by nearly six percentage points in the presidential election. Democratic Senate candidate Colin Allred also won the county by roughly 11 percentage points over Republican incumbent Ted Cruz.This year's Texas Senate contest has drawn national attention, with Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton facing Democratic candidate James Talarico. Republican Governor Greg Abbott is also seeking re-election against Democrat Gina Hinojosa.Early voting has also increased in other states with competitive Senate races. South Carolina, which Trump won by nearly 18 percentage points in the 2024 presidential election, has recorded an 83% rise in early voting compared with the 2022 midterms, as per AP analysis.In Kansas, where Republicans face another closely contested Senate race, early voting is up 34%. Maine has recorded a 44% increase, while Michigan has seen a rise of 32%, the AP reported.The midterm elections will determine the composition of the House of Representatives and Senate for the remaining two years of Trump's term. Rising prices of food, petrol and other essentials, the war involving Iran and concerns about government corruption have featured in the political debate ahead of the vote.Trump has held rallies across several states to support Republican candidates, including in areas that have traditionally been considered safe for the party. During his campaign appearances, he has repeatedly commented on candidates' physical appearance and dismissed concerns about rising petrol prices, pointing instead to the profits of fossil fuel companies.Speaking at a rally in Florida on Friday night, Trump acknowledged the demands of his campaign schedule.“I thought this was it,” he said. “I thought I could relax. Twenty-eight days of this crap in a row is a lot. It’s a lot.”You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: FREYJA missile shield: Ukraine's new bet against Russian ballistic missiles
articles.summary: Ukraine has completed its part of a new multinational missile defence system designed to intercept ballistic missiles, but the programme is still waiting
articles.body: Ukraine has completed its part of a new multinational missile defence system designed to intercept ballistic missiles, but the programme is still waiting for critical components from European partners before it can move towards testing. The development marks a major step in Kyiv's effort to build an alternative to US-made Patriot systems as Russia continues to intensify missile and drone attacks on Ukrainian cities.According to Defence News, the system, called FREYJA, is being developed through a coalition of Ukraine and European countries. Ukrainian defence company Fire Point has completed its assigned work on the FP-7.X interceptor and launcher, while European partners are responsible for supplying key technologies, including radar, infrared seekers and command-and-control systems.The programme is targeting initial testing by the end of 2026, with battlefield deployment planned for 2027. However, the timeline depends on the delivery and integration of the remaining European components."Ukraine has done what it was supposed to do, and that is good news," Zelenskyy told journalists, adding that 10 countries were participating in the programme and working on their respective contributions."People work on systems like this for decades. We want it very fast, because there is no time," he said, highlighting the urgency of developing an indigenous capability to intercept ballistic missiles.Which countries are involved and what are they contributing?The Integrated Anti-Ballistic Missile Coalition was formally established on July 13, 2026, in Paris. According to the joint declaration published by the Swedish government, its 10 founding members are Ukraine, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom.Ukraine is developing the FP-7.X interceptor missile and launcher through its defence company Fire Point. Germany is contributing radar technology through Hensoldt, including its TRML-4D radar, while Diehl Defence is involved in infrared seeker development. Norway's Kongsberg Defence and Aerospace is developing the command-and-control centre.Other potential technology suppliers include Sweden's Saab and France's Thales for long-range surveillance radar, and Denmark's Weibel Scientific and Italy's Leonardo for fire-control radar. These are proposed contributions in the preliminary design, not all confirmed contracts. Poland joined the coalition in September, while Canada has expressed readiness to contribute technology.How FREYJA will work and why Ukraine needs its own missile shieldFREYJA is being designed as an integrated ballistic missile defence network combining Ukraine's FP-7.X interceptor and launcher with European radar, tracking, guidance and command-and-control technologies.Its surveillance radars will detect incoming ballistic missiles, while tracking radars monitor their trajectory and relay information to a central command centre being developed by Norway's Kongsberg. The system will use NATO's Link 16 communication standard to connect with Ukraine's wider air defence network, while the Asterix protocol will facilitate radar-data exchange.The initial FP-7.X interceptor is designed to engage threats at an altitude of approximately 20 to 25 kilometres using a blast-fragmentation warhead, with a hit-to-kill version planned for the future. The architecture is modular, allowing components from different manufacturers to be integrated or replaced.Ukraine's push to develop FREYJA is driven by its growing dependence on the US-made Patriot air defence system to intercept Russian ballistic missiles. However, the supply of Patriot PAC-3 interceptors remains limited, with high production costs and growing international demand adding to the pressure.According to Defense News, a PAC-3 interceptor costs approximately $3.8 million, while Ukrainian defence company Fire Point is targeting a production cost of less than $1.2 million for its FP-7.X interceptor in serial production. The shortage has become more pressing after the US-Israel war with Iran depleted an estimated two-thirds of America's prewar PAC-3 interceptor stockpile.With Russia continuing to launch ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and large numbers of drones against Ukrainian cities, Kyiv wants to build a more affordable and sustainable missile defence capability.FREYJA could help Ukraine expand its interceptor supplies, reduce dependence on American weapons and strengthen its domestic defence industry through European technological cooperation.

articles.title: After 34 years caring for a Crufts-winning breeder's dogs, a Hampshire kennel worker challenged her £1.1m will despite receiving £100,000; her son agreed to raise his monthly support from £350 to £850
articles.summary: A long-serving kennel worker who spent 34 years caring for prize-winning Airedale terriers has taken his late employer’s son to court over her £1.1m
articles.body: A long-serving kennel worker who spent 34 years caring for prize-winning Airedale terriers has taken his late employer’s son to court over her £1.1m estate, arguing that the £100,000 left to him in her will was not enough to secure his future. The case has now led to an interim agreement under which the son will increase his monthly support from £350 to £850 while the dispute continues. The story, reported by The Independent, The Telegraph, The Times and the Daily Mail, centres on Mary Swash, a celebrated Hampshire breeder whose dogs achieved success at Crufts, and David Brand, the man who worked beside her for much of his adult life. Read more about it here:A life built around the kennelsMary Swash founded the Jokyl kennels in 1959 at her farm in West Tisted, near Alresford in Hampshire. Over the decades she became known internationally for breeding pedigree Airedale terriers, and her greatest show-ring triumph came in 1986 when her bitch, Ginger Christmas Carol, known at home as Emma, won Best in Show at Crufts.David Brand began living and working with Swash in 1992, when he was in his mid-twenties. He cared for her dogs, lived in accommodation on the farm and remained there after her death, looking after ten Airedales, six of which belong to her estate and four of which are his own. His lawyers told the High Court that he devoted his entire adult life to Swash’s kennels and that the arrangement was never simply an ordinary job.According to evidence heard in court, Swash provided Brand with his home, paid his bills, covered his food and vehicle costs and gave him £50 a week in pocket money. Her barrister said there was no formal employment contract and no conventional wage, describing the relationship instead as an informal arrangement that endured for 34 years. The judge, Deputy Master Michael Jefferis, accepted that this was not a commercial relationship and noted that Swash spoke of Brand as though he were family.The will and the claimSwash died aged 89 in July 2025. Her 2008 will, which was never changed, left Brand £100,000 and the remainder of her estate to her only son, John Cartledge. The estate consists mainly of the Hampshire farm, valued at £1.1m for probate in December, together with around £70,000 in cash.Brand later lodged a caveat freezing the estate’s assets and indicated that he would pursue a claim for reasonable financial provision under the Inheritance Act 1975. His case is that he was dependent on Swash and that she had promised to look after him for life. He also says he helped care for her during the final year of her life, alongside a professional carer.At a recent hearing in London’s High Court, Brand’s lawyers asked for either a £50,000 lump sum or £865 a month from the estate to support him until a full trial next year. They argued that he was in immediate need, had little money left and faced the winter while continuing to care for ten dogs. His counsel said the £300,000 accommodation offer made by Cartledge would not buy a suitable home in an expensive part of Hampshire, where Brand wished to remain.The son’s responseJohn Cartledge, Swash’s 63-year-old son and the executor of her estate, had already been paying Brand £350 a month. He was also providing food for the dogs and paying around £1,500 a month in estate expenses. In an email to Brand’s lawyers, he wrote that Brand would not be homeless and that he understood what he had meant to his mother, adding that it was his duty to ensure Brand lived comfortably for the rest of his life.Cartledge had also offered a more substantial settlement: buying Brand a £300,000 house with money from the estate, giving him the right to live there for life, on top of the £100,000 legacy. His lawyers argued that Brand’s claim could potentially consume the entire net value of the estate, leaving Cartledge with nothing from his mother’s will.After the hearing, however, Cartledge agreed to raise Brand’s monthly payments to £850, while continuing to meet around £1,500 a month in estate and dog-related expenses. The judge approved that undertaking, describing Cartledge as having been “quite generous” and saying he should be praised for recognising a responsibility to look after Brand.What the judge saidDeputy Master Jefferis found that Brand had a strong claim and an immediate need for support. He said the relationship between Swash and Brand was not merely that of employer and employee, pointing to the absence of a wage, the long-running informal arrangement and Swash’s stated hope that Brand would be settled in a house and looked after after her death.At the same time, the judge questioned whether £850 a month was perhaps on the generous side. He also asked why Brand could not seek other work, why caring for ten dogs should be treated as a full-time occupation, and why the dogs belonging to the estate could not be sold. Brand’s lawyers responded that the dogs were his companions and that rehoming them would be a cruel imposition on a man whose life had been built around them.A dispute about more than moneyThe case is ultimately about how the law should treat someone who was neither a family member in the formal sense nor an ordinary employee. Brand received a significant legacy, but he argues that a lifetime of unpaid or loosely paid care, combined with dependence on Swash for housing and daily needs, justifies a greater share of her estate.For Cartledge, the dispute is equally personal. He maintains that he has tried to avoid court and has offered meaningful support, yet his lawyers say the claim now being advanced could leave him with no economic interest in the estate. The full trial is expected next year, when the court will decide whether Brand’s needs justify a larger provision from Swash’s £1.1m fortune.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Attempted murder’: Molotov cocktail hits Paris police officer as France protests turn violent
articles.summary: A police officer was struck by a Molotov cocktail during clashes in Paris on Saturday, as demonstrations over rising living costs and deteriorating public
articles.body: A police officer was struck by a Molotov cocktail during clashes in Paris on Saturday, as demonstrations over rising living costs and deteriorating public services turned violent in several French cities.The interior ministry said 565 people had been arrested across France. Four police officers and one gendarme were injured in Paris, with three officers suffering burns from Molotov cocktails. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said around 150 planned demonstrations had passed off peacefully but condemned what he described as an “extraordinary” level of violence by some groups as the rallies ended.An estimated 320,000 people took part in demonstrations across the country, down from 410,000 the previous weekend, according to the interior ministry. Around 70,000 marched in Paris, where protesters set off from Porte de Bagnolet and headed towards Porte de Charenton, largely avoiding the city centre.The march was mostly peaceful until it reached its final destination. Dozens of masked people dressed in black used hammers to prise up paving stones and throw them at police, while at least one incendiary device was hurled at security forces, AFP journalists reported. Police responded with tear gas and baton charges. The Paris police prefecture said several hundred rioters had attacked officers with projectiles.The violence came despite a major security deployment. Nuñez had announced that 70,000 police officers and gendarmes, including elite units, would be deployed across the country, warning that Saturday was expected to be a high-risk day. He described the attack on the police officer with a Molotov cocktail as an “attempted murder”.Protests spread across EuropeThe demonstrations brought together school students, trade unions and Yellow Vest protesters, united by anger over the cost of living, widening inequalities and the state of public services under French president Emmanuel Macron’s government. Some protesters wore Halloween costumes, carrying placards and slogans reflecting their anger.In Lyon, clashes broke out after protesters threw projectiles at police, who responded with tear gas. In Toulouse, officers used water cannon against an unauthorised demonstration attended by several thousand people, mostly young protesters.Student groups said they planned further high school and university blockades on Tuesday and Thursday, before joining a demonstration called by workers and trade unions on November 5.In Germany, police used water cannon to disperse crowds after youth-led demonstrations organised by the group “Gen Z regelt!” turned violent in several cities. The rallies, held under the slogan of better education, healthcare, climate action and affordable living, had largely remained peaceful before clashes broke out towards the evening.In Frankfurt, at least two stores were looted and several others damaged, while police struggled to regain control, according to a Reuters witness. In Cologne, officers used water cannon after protesters allegedly targeted them with fireworks. In Berlin, demonstrators threw bottles and eggs, while protesters in Hamburg set barricades on fire, Bild reported.Fresh anti-government protests also took place in Albania’s capital, Tirana, where demonstrators renewed calls for Prime Minister Edi Rama to resign. A march outside the education ministry turned violent when masked youths threw paving stones and firebombs at police and set rubbish bins alight.Police were also on alert in Barcelona after an anonymous TikTok network called Blocus urged fresh gatherings, and in Italy following recent clashes in Milan, Turin and Bologna.You use AI every day. articles.title: A hospital employee in New Zealand diverted $1 million from patient payments by secretly changing bank details on documents; investigators identified unusual behaviour that helped expose the fraud
articles.summary: A hospital employee in New Zealand diverted more than $1 million in patient payments over 6 years by manipulating the organisation’s accounting system and
articles.body: A hospital employee in New Zealand diverted more than $1 million in patient payments over 6 years by manipulating the organisation’s accounting system and changing bank details on official documents. The money, which should have gone to Christchurch Hospital, was instead transferred to accounts controlled by the employee. The fraud came to light after a patient questioned an invoice for medical treatment they had already paid for. An investigation by the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) later revealed how the employee had exploited weaknesses in the hospital’s payment procedures while displaying unusual workplace behaviour.How did the hospital employee divert $1 million in patient paymentsAccording to a case study published by New Zealand’s Serious Fraud Office, the employee worked as an internal eligibility specialist at Christchurch Hospital, which was part of the Canterbury District Health Board. Her responsibilities included invoicing patients who were not eligible for publicly funded free healthcare and collecting payments for their treatment.The position gave her access to the hospital’s billing and payment processes. Over a 6-year period, she used that access to redirect 475 patient payments into bank accounts she controlled. The total financial loss to the hospital exceeded $1 million.The SFO identified several methods used to carry out the fraud. In some instances, the employee offered patients unauthorised discounts if they paid in cash, but kept the money instead of passing it to the hospital. She also created false invoices containing her own bank account details, making it appear that patients were paying through an official hospital process.Another method involved entering incorrect patient information into the hospital's system. By changing details, she made certain patients appear eligible for free healthcare, allowing her to manipulate the records associated with their treatment and payments.The employee also used a manual accounting process to remove outstanding debts from patients' accounts. Since this system did not record the changes made, the adjustments were difficult to identify. It also made some debts appear as though they had never existed.What brought the 6-year fraud to lightThe fraud was eventually uncovered after a patient contacted the hospital about an invoice for medical treatment that had already been paid for several months earlier.The patient's query prompted the hospital to examine the payment document. During the initial checks, staff discovered that the bank account listed on the invoice was not owned by the hospital. This raised concerns about whether the payment had reached its intended destination.Further enquiries uncovered additional emails sent by the employee to patients. These messages requested that patients transfer money directly into bank accounts that were not associated with the hospital.The discovery led to a more detailed internal examination of the payment records. With assistance from an external consultant, the hospital conducted an internal audit, which identified that the employee had been directing payments from patients who were required to pay for their treatment into accounts under her control.The findings were subsequently referred to the Serious Fraud Office for investigation. The employee was prosecuted and sentenced to 3 years in prison, according to the SFO case study.Unusual workplace behaviour raised further concernsThe investigation also highlighted several warning signs in the employee's conduct that could have attracted attention earlier.One unusual pattern was her reluctance to take time away from work. The SFO reported that she sometimes visited the office on days when she was not scheduled to work or even when she was officially on leave. Such behaviour allowed her to maintain control over tasks and processes that might otherwise have been handled by other employees.She also resisted sharing responsibilities with colleagues. In particular, she insisted that she should be the only person dealing with certain patients. This limited the involvement of other staff members and reduced the chances of someone independently checking her work.Another warning sign involved her communication with patients outside normal working hours. The employee contacted some patients through social media platforms, rather than relying exclusively on the hospital's usual communication channels.The SFO also identified a lack of oversight as an important factor. The employee had considerable control over the payment process, with little supervision or independent checking of the transactions she handled.Together, these behaviours created an environment in which irregular payments and altered records could continue without being noticed for an extended period.The fraud affected patients and hospital staff beyond the financial lossThe SFO reported that the financial loss exceeded $1 million, an amount that could have covered the salaries of 18 graduate nurses.Discovering that a colleague had manipulated internal processes and diverted patient payments affected staff members who were responsible for maintaining the organisation's financial operations.Patients were also placed in a vulnerable position. The employee had misused private information relating to sensitive medical procedures to identify and approach people who were less familiar with the costs associated with their treatment.Because these patients had limited knowledge of what they were required to pay, they could be more easily persuaded to transfer money into accounts presented as legitimate payment destinations.Hospital introduced changes to prevent similar fraudThe Canterbury District Health Board engaged a consultant who examined the existing financial controls and helped develop a new framework to reduce the risk of similar incidents.The hospital also reviewed its payment procedures and stopped accepting cash payments. This change was intended to reduce opportunities for employees to collect money directly from patients, without a record.In addition, the organisation increased internal fraud awareness and communicated information about the appropriate people and channels employees could contact if they suspected wrongdoing.Several measures that organisations can adopt include restricting access to sensitive financial information, introducing automatic systems that record changes to transactions and documents, and ensuring that unauthorised individuals cannot alter official records.You use AI every day. articles.title: A 400-acre wildlife preserve in Sonoma County began with Peter Lang, who kept exotic animals on a Beverly Hills cattle ranch in the 1970s; five decades later, Safari West is being handed to a nonprofit to carry on his conservation work
articles.summary: Giraffes graze in the open grasslands in the hills of Sonoma County. Rhinos pad around their enclosures. Flamingos add a splash of color to the scenery.
articles.body: Giraffes graze in the open grasslands in the hills of Sonoma County. Rhinos pad around their enclosures. Flamingos add a splash of color to the scenery. For over thirty years, Safari West has been bringing a taste of the African wilderness to California. But behind the popular wildlife attraction is the story of one man's passion for exotic animals, a family's dedication to conservation and one nite when everything they had built almost came to be lost. Now the 400-acre preserve is set for another transformation, from private to nonprofit stewardship, to secure its future.Fascination was turned into a life missionAccording to Visit California, the Safari West story starts in the 1970’s when Peter Lang, owner of a cattle ranch in Beverly Hills, became interested in exotic animals. In the 1980s he bought a former cattle ranch in Sonoma County to enlarge his private collection of animals. With his wife, the zoologist Nancy Lang, he began to make better use of the property, setting up a captive breeding program with the main goal of conservation. In 1993 the preserve opened to the public and was nicknamed the “Sonoma Serengeti.” Today it is home to more than 900 animals including giraffes, rhinoceroses, cheetahs, zebras, lemurs, monkeys and flamingos, according to KRON4 News.The whole nite was at stakeThe preserve's commitment to its animals was tested during the Tubbs Fire in October 2017. Wildfires swept through Sonoma County and Lang evacuated his wife, guests and staff. But he lingered behind. The then 77-year-old spent the nite wandering around the property with garden hoses and shovels to battle fires caused by flying embers, Visit California says. He also moved animals between pens and took flammable materials out of the way so the flames would not spread.The four houses in the Lang family compound were destroyed, but Safari West suffered little damage. Several fences, vehicles, smaller buildings and old oak trees were damaged but no animals were injured. The preserve reopened Nov. 20, 2017, after the threat was no longer imminent.The next chapter for Safari WestAlmost ten years later, the preserve is at a new crossroads. As KRON4 News reported, Safari West will convert from a 35-year-old privately held business to a California nonprofit public benefit corporation. The change is intended to increase work on research, education and conservation, while allowing the property to remain open to visitors. The safari tours, tent accommodation overnight stay and wildlife education programs are expected to continue under the same leadership and dedicated team. A state employment filing says 134 employees will be laid off, but they’re expected to be hired back under the new nonprofit structure.Continuing the legacyMuch of what you’ll see at Safari West is not new to visitors. Large room. The open-air Jeep tours will continue to roam the expansive property where guests will encounter animals roaming its grasslands and wooded habitats. Overnight guests will also get to experience the preserve, from safari-style tent cabins.The nonprofit ownership model provides Safari West a new structure to continue the work that Peter and Nancy Lang began decades ago. What was once a private obsession with exotic wildlife is now a conservation destination, and the next chapter is all about ensuring that legacy continues beyond its founders.Image Courtesy: John Burgess / The Press DemocratYou use AI every day. articles.title: Inside UK PM’s Diwali party at his residence; from Gita chanting to vegetarian snacks, woman shares interesting details
articles.summary: A Diwali reception at 10 Downing Street gave travel creator Shanu, who goes by @shinewithshanu on Instagram, an opportunity to see how the festival was
articles.body: A Diwali reception at 10 Downing Street gave travel creator Shanu, who goes by @shinewithshanu on Instagram, an opportunity to see how the festival was celebrated at the official residence of the UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. From flower decorations, diyas and rangolis to vegetarian food, Bhagavad Gita recitation and the chanting of the Hare Krishna Mahamantra, she shared details of the evening in a video posted on Instagram.“Come celebrate Diwali with me at the UK Prime Minister's residence, 10 Downing Street, and you're going to be amazed. I'm so honoured to have been invited to the UK PM's Diwali reception,” she said at the beginning of the video.After completing the security checks, Shanu entered the historic residence and showed viewers the decorations arranged for the occasion. The rooms featured flowers, diyas, rangolis and a murti of Lord Ganesha. “We are inside and I'm absolutely awestruck by how beautifully everything was decorated for Diwali. There were gorgeous flower decorations, Ganesh ji's murti, diyas, and beautiful rangolis. The entire place was glowing with the beauty of Diwali,” she said.She also showed the iconic staircase at 10 Downing Street, where generations of British prime ministers have walked. From there, she took viewers into a hall where dignitaries had gathered for the reception.Vegetarian food, Diwali rituals and the Prime Minister's arrivalShanu said she enjoyed the vegetarian food and soft drinks served at the event. She then waited for the Prime Minister to arrive. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham arrived with his wife. The couple lit the ceremonial diya, after which the gathering observed religious rituals that included a recitation from the Bhagavad Gita and chanting of the Hare Krishna Mahamantra. The programme also included the singing of the Hanuman Chalisa.Starmer then addressed the guests and acknowledged the contributions of people working in their communities and public services. “Namaste, Shubh Diwali. Everyone, more importantly, thank you for everything that you are doing in your communities to support people, to bring people together, to work in our health service, in our public services,” he said.He also spoke about his government's support for community work, adding, “And I can assure you that the government will continue to back you in everything that we do.”The Prime Minister then referred to the UK's relationship with India. “I can say that as Prime Minister I will be building the strongest possible links with India. Shubh Diwali, everybody. Have a wonderful evening,” he said.Burnham praises the Diwali decorations at Downing StreetTowards the end of the event, Andy Burnham also commented on how the residence had been decorated for the festival. “Enjoy the light. Enjoy Downing Street looking at it, sir. I don't remember it looking this amazing at any time. So well done of everybody who's made it, brought it to life in this way. Happy Diwali, everybody. It's wonderful to be here,” he said.Shanu ended her video by expressing gratitude for being part of the celebration. “I feel so blessed to have been part of such a beautiful Diwali celebration,” she said. Sharing the video, she captioned it: “Diwali Celebrations at the UK Prime Minister’s Residence, 10 Downing Street. Some dreams really do come true!”Her video offered a glimpse of the Diwali reception through the eyes of an invited guest, documenting the decorations, food, religious observances and the Prime Minister's address at one of Britain's most recognisable official residences.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc on Sunday held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Leaders of the INDIA bloc on Sunday held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, targeting Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The rally held over allegations of “vote chori”, saw senior INDIA bloc leaders accuse the BJP of electoral manipulation and undermining democratic institutions.Several opposition leaders targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission was favouring the ruling party.They demanded Kumar's removal and vowed to continue their campaign against him.'Gyanesh, when will you vanish?' Mamata mocks CECFormer West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of trying to influence the West Bengal elections and vowed to fight against the alleged actions.“Bengal is victim of SIR. We will not spare them, we will fight,” she said, adding, “Gyanesh, when will you vanish?”Mamata also accused the BJP of looting funds linked to the Ram Janmabhoomi and Waqf properties, and alleged that the police had become the party's “comrades”.“What haven't they looted? They looted the money of Ram Janmabhoomi, Waqf properties... The police became their comrades. The BJP has no organisation of its own. That is why they make the police do party work. Agencies don't work with the BJP. The BJP will go,” she said.Accusing the BJP of undermining democracy and the Constitution through alleged “vote theft”, Mamata said the party had also deprived young people of jobs, compromised women's dignity and misused donations.“These people have looted the country's democracy and constitution through 'vote theft', and attacked it on top of that. The BJP has stolen youth's jobs, stolen women's honor, stolen donations—we must remove them from power,” she said.“Bengal is the victim of the circumstances of this SIR. We will not give up. We will give our lives, we will fight, but we will not surrender. They looted our Bengal. We will save democracy and bring it back... We will take revenge through politics. We will take revenge through democracy. We will fight...” she added.'After Gyanesh, you're next': Rahul warns PM Modi, ShahLeader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar, alleging that the Election Commission had helped the BJP manipulate elections.“Listen to me. What I say always turns out to be true, doesn't it? I am telling every citizen and every youth of India: Gyanesh Kumar will be removed from the post of Chief Election Commissioner. Gyanesh Kumar will go to jail,” he said.He also alleged that PM Modi and Amit Shah would not have reached their current positions without Kumar's help. “Without Gyanesh Kumar, neither Narendra Modi would have become Prime Minister nor Amit Shah would have become Home Minister,” Rahul said.Rahul said the opposition was not driven by hatred towards the BJP leadership but was fighting to protect the Constitution and the rights of citizens.“We do not hate Narendra Modi, Amit Shah or Gyanesh Kumar. We are people who open the shop of love, not hatred. We are people of non-violence. For me, there is no enemy. Neither Narendra Modi, nor Amit Shah, nor Gyanesh Kumar. But the voice of every citizen of India is more important to me, even more important than religion. That is my religion,” he said.He added that the INDIA bloc would not resort to violence or spread hatred but would continue to oppose any attempt to undermine the Constitution.“We will not use violence, we will not harm anyone and we will not spread hatred. We will work with love. But we will not let you destroy the Constitution. No matter what happens, we will not let it happen,” Rahul said.Rahul also raised concerns over unemployment, farmers' rights and the concentration of wealth, alleging that the country's resources were increasingly in the hands of a few people.“The farmer is not getting his rights. The youth are not getting employment. The labourer is not getting his rights, and the entire wealth has gone into the hands of two or three people. We do not want such an India, and we will not accept such an India,” he said.He said the country should ensure that farmers received the benefits of their hard work and that students who worked hard had access to employment.“Anyone can join Shiv ki Baraat. Every living being can join it. Can anyone be stopped from participating in that? No. We want that kind of India. If a farmer works hard, he should reap the rewards. If a student studies for 18 hours, they should get employment. We do not want a country that belongs only to two or three people,” Rahul said.Referring to Amit Shah's remarks that PM Modi would remain in power, Rahul said the opposition would continue its campaign after demanding action against the CEC.“Amit Shah ji said Narendra Modi is not going anywhere. I am telling you the opposite: Narendra Modi cannot go anywhere. Even if he wants to leave, we will not let him go. After Gyanesh Kumar, we are going to stand right in front of you. Legal action will be taken against them,” he said.Rahul described Kumar's removal as the first step towards putting the country back on the right track. “The first step to get the country back on the right track is to remove Gyanesh Kumar,” he said.Kharge accuses Modi, Shah of shielding CECCongress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged that the BJP government had come to power through a “stolen” mandate. He said removing Prime Minister Narendra Modi was necessary to protect democracy.Kharge accused Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of attempting to take away the voting rights of Dalits, women and young people. He alleged that the two leaders were shielding CEC Gyanesh Kumar.“Modi and Shah have attempted to snatch the vote of Dalits, youth and women. Modi ji wants to take away their votes through his man -- Ganesh Kumar. We will keep fighting until he goes, and ensure his exit,” Kharge said.He further alleged that the BJP-led governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh had been formed through “vote chori”.“Be it the central government, governments in Maharashtra, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, they are 'chori' governments (formed on stolen mandate). We have to throw out these 'vote chor',” he said.Kharge also said the opposition would continue its agitation until Kumar resigned.“No matter how many attempts Narendra Modi makes.. until Gyanesh Kumar resigns, we will not stay silent—we will keep fighting,” he said.He added that opposition leaders would not be intimidated by central agencies or the police.“We have the strength to fight and will not be intimidated by the police, CBI, ED or any other government agency. Neither will our INDIA alliance leaders be scared. Everyone on this stage is ready to fight,” Kharge said.He also reiterated his call for Modi's removal, saying: “Modi jayega to hi loktantra bachega, Modi ko hatayenge tabhi loktantra ko bachenyenge, Modi ko hatao loktantra ko bachao (Remove Modi to save democracy).”Akhilesh invokes Haldighati, predicts ‘parivartan’Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav described Ramlila Maidan as the “Haldighati of democracy” and said the rally signalled that political change could come at any time.“Today, Ramlila Maidan has turned into the Haldighati of democracy. The massive public support and slogans of revolution are proof that change can happen at any moment,” he said.Akhilesh also targeted the BJP, saying those who had once claimed to be an “unmovable foot of Angad” had lost their political ground.He alleged that the party was turning to the Election Commission because it feared losing elections.“The people of UP know how to welcome and how to bid farewell even better. In 2027, such a farewell will happen that the Bharatiya Janata Party and its allies will not be able to return again,” he added.Tejashwi compares rally to MahabharataRashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) leader Tejashwi Yadav compared the opposition rally to the Mahabharata, accusing those in power of manipulating elections.“While the Ramlila Maidan is traditionally meant for staging the Ramayana, today we have organised a 'Mahabharata' for those who steal votes,” he said.Referring to the dice game in the epic, Tejashwi said, “You are all aware of the game Shakuni played in the Mahabharata. You know your history: the Mahabharata began not on a battlefield, but with a game of dice. And now that Shakuni is playing his game, we are compelled to fight the battle...”Several senior opposition leaders attended the rally, including Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, Mamata Banerjee, CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby, CPI general secretary D Raja and CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya.Earlier, INDIA bloc leaders travelled in an open vehicle from the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction towards Ramlila Maidan, as hundreds of supporters marched alongside them.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Chacha, come for refreshments': UP senior advocate lured into car, abducted and murdered
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: A senior advocate and four-time former president of the Kalpi Bar Association, Gayadin Ahirwar (70), was allegedly abducted and murdered after
articles.body: LUCKNOW: A senior advocate and four-time former president of the Kalpi Bar Association, Gayadin Ahirwar (70), was allegedly abducted and murdered after being lured into a car by men posing as clients seeking to discuss a case.His body was recovered from Kanpur Nagar's Sachendi area on Sunday morning, hours after he went missing while returning home from court.Police have detained three suspects and are questioning them to unravel the conspiracy behind the killing.Preliminary investigations indicate that a long-running land dispute may have been the motive, though officials said all angles are being examined.According to family members, Ahirwar had attended proceedings at the Orai court on Saturday and called his son, Harsh Mitra, around 3.30 pm, asking him to pick him up from Munna Full Power intersection. He reportedly told his son they needed to collect a legal file from a client near the Durga Temple crossing before heading home.Harsh took his father to the designated location on a scooter. There, a white Maruti Dzire with three occupants was waiting.According to the family, two men stepped out, addressed the advocate as "Chacha" and asked him to accompany them for refreshments before handing over the case file. Trusting them, Ahirwar got into the vehicle, which then drove towards Alampur crossing.Harsh followed the car for some distance but eventually lost sight of it. When his father failed to return home and his mobile phone became unreachable, the family alerted police.Jalaun police launched a large-scale overnight search operation.Superintendent of police Suresh Chandra Rawat said multiple teams were deployed and technical surveillance, including CCTV footage analysis, was used to track the victim and the vehicle.The breakthrough came during the night when police detained three suspects. Based on information gathered during interrogation, teams traced Ahirwar's body to the Gujaini Park area under Sachendi police station limits in Kanpur Nagar, nearly 80-90 kilometres from Kalpi.Police sources said the advocate had suffered multiple injuries on his head, face and back, while one eye had been severely damaged, indicating a brutal assault before death. The body was sent for post-mortem examination.Investigators are closely scrutinising a decades-old dispute involving nearly four hectares of land in Hasa village under Kalpi tehsil.Fellow advocates said Ahirwar had been locked in litigation over the property since 2000, with several civil and consolidation cases pending before courts. The property was later allegedly sold during the dispute, triggering further legal battles and stay orders.Police are also examining an SC/ST Act case filed by Ahirwar against several individuals, including a land claimant, following an alleged assault. The matter had come up for hearing in Orai on October 31, and the next date was fixed for November 11. Ahirwar was returning from that hearing when he was allegedly abducted.A prominent legal practitioner since 1981, Ahirwar was elected president of the Kalpi Bar Association for a fourth term earlier this year.
