articles.title: 'Stay quiet or I'll speak for an hour': Kharge's playful warning to supporters at Ramlila Maidan rally
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had a humorous exchange with supporters at the INDIA bloc's mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had a humorous exchange with supporters at the INDIA bloc's mega rally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi on Sunday. During his address, he warned that he could turn his five-minute speech into an hour-long address if the crowd did not quieten down.As supporters began making noise while he was speaking, Kharge paused to tell them, "Dekho aap agar chup baithenge, main 5 min mei apna bhaashan khatam kar raha hoon. Aap chup nahi baithenge, main 1 ghanta apna bhaashan karunga."The remark comes amid the opposition's show of strength against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Several INDIA bloc leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, attended the rally.The Congress chief also launched a sharp attack on the BJP, accusing its governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh of coming to power through what he called "vote theft". He called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi's removal, saying democracy could survive only if he left office."Who votes for them? They choose themselves. The public does not elect them. The current central government, as well as the governments in Maharashtra, Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, are all governments of vote theft. We must remove these thieves," Kharge said."Only if Modi goes will democracy survive. We must remove Modi to save democracy," he added.Kharge also said the opposition would fight together to remove Modi, protect the Constitution, strengthen democracy and save the country.The rally was part of the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Delhi' protest march. Opposition leaders and supporters from across the country gathered to raise concerns over the SIR exercise and alleged irregularities in electoral rolls.The march began at the Minto Road-Connaught Place junction and proceeded towards Ramlila Maidan. It followed a public 'impeachment' programme against the CEC held in the capital on October 31.Meanwhile, BJP leader and Sambalpur MP Dharmendra Pradhan took part in the party's 'Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao' (Save Democracy, End Anarchy) padayatra in Faridabad on Sunday. He accused Rahul Gandhi and the Congress of losing faith in democratic institutions.Pradhan was accompanied by Union minister of state Krishan Pal Gurjar, minister of state Rajesh Nagar, Haryana sports minister Gaurav Gautam, several MLAs and party workers. The march was part of the BJP's nationwide campaign.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Rahul's Ramlila 'jalsa' to 'rub salt in wounds' of 1984 Sikh riot victims: Amit Shah
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday staunchly criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for holding an INDIA bloc rally in Delhi's Ramlila
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday staunchly criticised Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for holding an INDIA bloc rally in Delhi's Ramlila Round on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.He said the "jalsa" would reopen painful memories for the victims and their families, accusing the Congress of showing little sensitivity towards the tragedy.Shah made the remarks in Chandigarh while addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for development projects worth Rs 258 crore."Rahul Gandhi's November 1 'jalsa' in Delhi will only rub salt in wounds of anti-Sikh riot victims," Shah was quoted as saying by the news agency PTI.The INDIA bloc held its 'Chalo Dilli' protest at Ramlila Maidan as part of its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Shah invokes memories of 1984 riotsTargeting the Congress over the violence, Shah said thousands of Sikhs were killed in Delhi on November 1, 1984. He recalled how families were torn apart, with people burnt alive, children orphaned, women widowed and homes destroyed.“The day the Sikh genocide happened, on that very day, they had to hold a rally,” Shah said, criticising the INDIA bloc for choosing the date for its protest.He also referred to a statement made by then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi after the killings, saying he had watched it on television and could never forget it."And the then Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi gave a statement and I saw that on TV and I cannot forget that for rest of my life. He had said when a big tree falls, the earth shakes," he said.Shah added that only Congress leaders could make such a remark after thousands of Sikhs had been killed. He also said the Modi government reopened cases linked to the 1984 riots after coming to power in 2014, provided compensation of Rs 5 lakh to the next of kin of each victim and jailed prominent Congress leaders.“India has never witnessed, nor will it ever witness, riots of this kind, incited by a political party,” Shah said.'Stay in mock Parliament if you want to be PM'Shah also targeted Rahul Gandhi over the INDIA bloc's symbolic proceedings against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. On Saturday, opposition parties had held a mock 'public impeachment' of the poll panel chief, accusing him of facilitating electoral irregularities and demanding action against him.Taking a swipe at Gandhi's political ambitions, Shah said the Congress leader should continue holding mock Parliament sessions if he wanted to become Prime Minister."If you want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life. Your turn won't come," Shah said.He also referred to Gandhi's electoral defeats and took a dig at Sonia Gandhi's reported ambition to see her son become Prime Minister.Shah accused the opposition of disrupting Parliament, spreading falsehoods and creating disorder. He said such conduct would keep the INDIA bloc out of power.“Telling lies, spreading anarchy, not letting Parliament function, this is your 'fitrat' (true nature),” Shah said of the opposition.He also described Rahul Gandhi's 'mohabbat ki dukaan' slogan as a message of hatred, arguing that holding the rally on the anniversary of the 1984 riots showed a lack of sensitivity towards the victims.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: After losing Celebrity Traitors, Maya Jama donated £83,500 of her own money to Action for Children, matching what she could have won to support families in need
articles.summary: Maya Jama has donated £83,500 of her own money to her chosen charity, Action for Children.
articles.body: Maya Jama has donated £83,500 of her own money to her chosen charity, Action for Children. The amount matches exactly what she would have won if she had claimed victory on the BBC reality show Celebrity Traitors. The 32-year-old Love Island host made it to the final episode of the second series but was voted out at the last stage by her fellow contestants. Although she missed out on the prize money, she decided to donate the full amount herself to help children and families in need across the UK.Personal gesture matches full final prize shareJama shared her decision on social media after the final episode aired on Friday night. In a post on X, the television presenter wrote: "Just donated what I would have won for my chosen charity @ActnForChildren. Amazing cause." Action for Children confirmed shortly afterwards that it had received the £83,500 donation. The charity helps children and young people facing poverty, abuse and housing problems. It also supports children who need foster care. Katherine Woods, director of fundraising at Action for Children, told the Press Association: "We're absolutely thrilled to receive such a generous donation from Maya Jama. She certainly held her nerve until the very end and proved herself to be the star of the show."Narrow defeat in the castle turretDuring the BBC series, Jama played one of the Traitors inside the Scottish castle. She managed to avoid being caught at several roundtables. However, her time in the game ended during the final. Fellow Traitor King Kenny voted against her at the last roundtable, revealing her true role to the other players. Speaking about her exit shortly before the final stage of the game, Jama said she was proud of how she handled the pressure. "I knew it was coming," Jama said. "I'm proud of myself for keeping composed and being 98 per cent myself the whole time. Obviously keeping a massive secret is so tough, but I think I did it well, and I'm really proud of that. She's out." Her exit left Faithful contestants Sebastian Croft and Romesh Ranganathan to go on and win the competition.Final outcome splits earnings for rival causesAfter Jama was voted out, actor Sebastian Croft and comedian Romesh Ranganathan became the final two contestants. They won the £83,000 prize pot and shared it between their chosen charities. Croft, best known for his role in Heartstopper, donated his £41,500 share of the official prize money to the humanitarian charity Choose Love. Meanwhile, Ranganathan gave his half of the winnings to the Refugee Council. The second series of Celebrity Traitors ended with record-breaking viewing figures for the BBC. Official figures released by the broadcaster showed that the final attracted an average overnight audience of 11.2 million viewers. This made it the most-watched episode of the format in UK history.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Florida couple allegedly used gunfire, chainsaws and airboat engines during weddings at a neighbouring 42-room historic mansion; an October 30 appeals court has now overturned an order meant to stop the disruptions
articles.summary: A Florida appeals court has overturned an order that aimed to stop a couple from disturbing outdoor wedding ceremonies at a neighbouring historic mansion.
articles.body: A Florida appeals court has overturned an order that aimed to stop a couple from disturbing outdoor wedding ceremonies at a neighbouring historic mansion. According to legal documents published by Justia Law, the Sixth District Court of Appeal issued its ruling on 30 October, overturning an order made by a lower court against the neighbouring property owners. The legal dispute centres on claims that the couple deliberately used loud equipment, including gunfire, chainsaws and revved-up airboat engines, to disrupt events at the nearby 42-room historic estate. The historic mansion is a popular venue for outdoor weddings and major social events. The estate's owners had previously received a temporary court order limiting noise and disruptive activities on the neighbouring property during scheduled events.Appellate decision reverses court restrictionsIn its ruling, the Sixth District Court of Appeal found that the lower court's order did not meet the legal and evidence requirements under Florida law. The appeal judges said the restrictions were too broad and unfairly limited how the neighbouring owners could use their own land without enough legal reason. The court noted that property owners have the right to enjoy their land peacefully. However, any court order limiting another person's activities must be specific and backed by strong evidence of an unlawful nuisance. The appeals court decided that the lower court had gone too far with its restrictions and cancelled the order. The dispute shows the tensions that can arise in rural and semi-rural parts of Florida, where businesses that host events operate next to private homes.Allegations of deliberate disturbanceCourt records describe a long history of disagreements between the estate owners and their neighbours. According to documents referred to in the appeals court's decision, the estate's management claimed that the neighbours deliberately planned noisy activities to take place during wedding vows and outdoor receptions. The legal case listed several examples of the alleged behaviour. These included firing weapons, using chainsaws along the property boundaries and running airboat engines without mufflers for long periods during weekend wedding ceremonies. The estate owners said these actions were deliberate and caused financial losses, disrupted private events and harmed the historic venue's reputation. The defence argued that the activities took place on private property and were allowed under normal property rights. It also challenged the legal basis for the court order restricting the neighbours' activities.Legal options remaining for estate ownersThe Sixth District Court of Appeal's decision sends the case back to the lower circuit court for further proceedings. Although the ruling removes the immediate restrictions on the neighbours, it does not bring the entire lawsuit to an end. Legal experts say the estate owners can still bring civil nuisance claims or ask the court for a revised order that meets the evidence requirements set out by the appeals court. However, any new restrictions will need clearer proof that the neighbours deliberately caused a nuisance. They will also need to be more specific about which activities are restricted. The circuit court has not yet announced a date for the next hearings, which will deal with the remaining claims between the two sides.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A sculptor transformed solid marble into the delicate illusion of a veiled woman's face; newly attributed to Antonio Corradini, the Baroque marble piece sold for a record €1.925 million at auction in Vienna, soaring past its high estimate of €16,000
articles.summary: Your first look is all admiration. The face is calm, the lines are soft, and the veil is as translucent as it can get.
articles.body: Your first look is all admiration. The face is calm, the lines are soft, and the veil is as translucent as it can get. The second look is accompanied by a question: how does a hard white stone turn into something that looks like cloth? By the time that question settles, you have stopped asking it. You are just standing there, a little more amazed than before.A marble sculpture of a woman wearing a veil was sold for €1.925 million (around €1.9 million) at an auction in Vienna on 20 October, setting a new world record for a work by the Italian Baroque sculptor Antonio Corradini. Several bidders in the saleroom and on the telephone tried their best to take home the highly coveted sculpture of a veiled lady, the auction house Dorotheum said.A face under a veilThe sculpture depicts a veiled woman carved in white marble. It stands 60 centimetres tall and is set on its own base. Veiled women were Corradini’s trademark, and this piece follows that pattern. The veil falls over the face without hiding it. The marble veil looks like soft fabric, demonstrating the patience, technique and artistry that went into the carving.Corradini was born in Venice in 1688. Sculptures from his workshop reached Dresden and St Petersburg before he ever left Italy. His patrons included King Augustus the Strong and Tsar Peter the Great.Corradini later spent about a decade in Vienna as court sculptor to Emperor Charles VI. Some of his work still stands in the city. A statue of Charles VI attributed to the artist can be found in the State Hall of the Austrian National Library. The figures on the Marriage Fountain on the Hoher Markt are among his best-known works. Dorotheum now considers the veiled lady definitively attributable to Antonio Corradini.A plaster model of the same bust is kept at the Ca’ Rezzonico museum in Venice. Conservators recently restored it as part of the Save Venice project. The model gives researchers something to compare with the marble.The auction drew interest from bidders in the saleroom and on the telephone. None of those present in the room managed to take it home. “The bidding ultimately ended in favour of a telephone bidder,” the auction house said in a press release. The price of €1.925 million set a new world record for Corradini and was far above the auction house’s estimate. The sculpture had been estimated to fetch between €12,000 and €16,000. The buyer's identity is currently unknown.The lucky buyer now owns a unique piece of art that looks lifelike. Three centuries after it was carved, the sculpture still poses the same question to anyone who looks at it closely: how did someone make marble look like cloth?You use AI every day. articles.title: 'I've never called you': Comedian Bill Maher mocks Trump over White House dinner row
articles.summary: Comedian Bill Maher has hit back at US President Donald Trump after the latter called him a “complete and total loser” in a lengthy Truth Social post,
articles.body: Comedian Bill Maher has hit back at US President Donald Trump after the latter called him a “complete and total loser” in a lengthy Truth Social post, using his television show to mock the President and dispute several claims about their White House dinner.During Friday's episode of HBO's 'Real Time with Bill Maher', the comedian responded to Trump's 1,318-word post, joking about its contents and explaining why he believed their conversations in person had been different from the President's public remarks.According to The Hollywood Reporter, Maher began by referring to the dinner and former President Barack Obama's recent comparison of Trump's White House to a Cheesecake Factory opened by Saddam Hussein.“And the Republicans all said, ‘Leave the Cheesecake Factory out of this!’ Well, I mean, I should know. I just had dinner there. I hear it went well. What have you heard?” Maher joked.He then turned to Trump's lengthy post, saying, “Now, did you see the 1,300-word Tweet he sent out? Longest ever. Kind of a flex.”Taking another dig at the President, Maher said, “dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory. After you leave, they review you.”Maher disputes Trump's claimsMaher also mocked the personal nature of Trump's criticism, saying, “He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store.”Reading excerpts from the post, the comedian said their dinners were meant to allow them to exchange views, disagree and listen to each other, rather than turn their differences into personal attacks.“Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree, but listen, which he does in person, but don’t hate each other. And then I go back to my job here and then the heartaches begin,” he said.One point Maher challenged was Trump's claim that he did not support taking nuclear weapons away from Iran. The comedian said the President had misunderstood his position and played clips from his programme to explain what he had said.He also rejected Trump's assertion that he repeatedly called the President.“Page two, he talks about how I call him incessantly. I’ve never called you, you call me. I’d be afraid to call you. You’re the president. I think you’re too busy. Well, plainly not.”'Major POTHEAD' remark draws a jokeTrump had also referred to Maher as a “major POTHEAD” in his post. The comedian responded with humour, saying, “Well, I guess the cat’s out of the bag now. Boy, that explains a lot. I thought I was just happy.”The President had additionally mentioned that Maher was carrying alcohol while walking through the White House during their dinner. Maher read out Trump's account, including his concluding remark that he had thought the meeting went well.Trump's post also discussed Maher's friendship with producer Chuck LaBella. He claimed LaBella and musician Kid Rock had repeatedly contacted him to arrange a meeting with the comedian, The Hollywood Reporter reported.According to Trump, their first dinner took place in March 2025 after those requests. The President also criticised Maher's HBO programme and its ratings.Maher and Trump had previously met for dinner at the White House, with Kid Rock also present. The latest exchange has brought that meeting back into public focus, with the comedian now offering his account of what happened and responding to the President's criticism.You use AI every day. articles.title: WWE Hall of Famer The Fabulous Moolah’s former 9.11-acre South Carolina estate is up for sale after its 2 houses and 6 smaller residences were demolished, leaving two ponds and wooded grounds
articles.summary: A property in Northeast Columbia, South Carolina, once associated with professional wrestling legend The Fabulous Moolah, is being offered for sale with
articles.body: A property in Northeast Columbia, South Carolina, once associated with professional wrestling legend The Fabulous Moolah, is being offered for sale with its former residential buildings already removed. The land, which spent years as the longtime home of the WWE Hall of Famer, is now being marketed as a redevelopment opportunity. As reported by The Realtor, its previous layout included two larger houses overlooking a pond and six smaller efficiency residences. None of those homes remain. Instead, the site is being presented to prospective buyers as a largely cleared parcel, with its existing landscape, water features and location among the main selling points. Three storage buildings are still standing on the property.The Fabulous Moolah’s wrestling legacy and her longtime Columbia homeThe property's connection to The Fabulous Moolah gives it a place in Columbia's local history. articles.title: Rs 5,000 UPI trail, cybercafe CCTV help Delhi Police rescue 13-year-old within 3 hours
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A Rs 5,000 UPI transfer that served as a digital trail, the cooperation of a cybercafe owner and a trap laid in a narrow lane in Karawal Nagar
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A Rs 5,000 UPI transfer that served as a digital trail, the cooperation of a cybercafe owner and a trap laid in a narrow lane in Karawal Nagar helped Delhi Police rescue a 13-year-old boy and arrest his kidnapper within three hours of his mother reporting his disappearance.The accused, identified as Akash, had allegedly kidnapped the boy and demanded a ransom of Rs 40,000.Police arrested him within three hours of receiving information, when he returned to collect the ransom after the Rs 5,000 UPI transfer at a cybercafe in Karawal Nagar, a police officer said on Sunday.The incident came to light on October 30, when a woman approached Jyoti Nagar police station in Shahdara and reported that her son had gone out to buy some items but had not returned."She subsequently received a call from an unidentified person demanding Rs 40,000 for his release. A case was registered, and a team was constituted to trace the child and apprehend the accused," the officer said.During the investigation, the kidnapper contacted the woman again and insisted that the ransom be paid through UPI. He sent her a barcode, following which police transferred Rs 5,000 using the account of a police personnel to trace the transaction."Technical surveillance led the investigators to a cybercafe in Karawal Nagar, where the owner disclosed that a man, accompanied by a minor boy, had used his UPI barcode to receive Rs 5,000 in exchange for a commission of Rs 50," the officer added.Police then examined the cybercafe's CCTV footage, which the woman used to identify her missing son."We then initiated another transaction of Rs 5,000 through the same barcode to lure the accused to come again to the same place," he said.The accused returned to the cybercafe with the boy to collect the money in cash. With the cafe owner's assistance, police personnel apprehended him and rescued the child safely.During interrogation, Akash told police that he worked as a delivery helper in Sadar Bazar and knew the victim through his cousin. He had allegedly lured the boy onto his scooter before calling his mother to demand ransom, police said.Police recovered Rs 5,000 in cash, the mobile phone allegedly used to make the ransom call and the scooter used in the kidnapping. The cafe owner had also received Rs 50 as commission for facilitating the transaction.Police said the accused had no previous criminal involvement and that the rescued boy had been reunited with his family.They are also investigating whether the accused planned the kidnapping alone or had help from anyone else.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Over 1k monks join robe offering ceremony at Mahabodhi Mahavihara in Bodh Gaya
articles.summary: Over 1,000 monks from Buddhist countries joined the Maha Kathina robe-offering ceremony at Bodh Gaya’s Mahabodhi Mahavihara; officials plan for crowds.
articles.body: Gaya: More than 1,000 monks from Thailand, Vietnam, Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Myanmar and other Buddhist countries took part in the Maha Kathina Civara Dana (robe-offering) ceremony under the sacred Bodhi tree at the Mahabodhi Mahavihara on Sunday. The event was organised by the Bodh Gaya Temple Management Committee (BTMC).Mahavihara caretaker monk Bhikkhu Manoj said the ceremony marks the end of Varshawaas (rainy retreat), a three-month period from July to Sept during which monks remain at their monasteries for meditation and prayers. As per Buddhist tradition, devotees offer new robes and other essentials to monks after the retreat.With the conclusion of the ceremony, the Mahavihara is set to host a series of major events organised by Buddhist groups from different countries. These include the 15-day fifth Vietnamese Tipitaka Chanting from Nov 14 to 28, the 11-day 21st International Tipitaka Chanting Ceremony from Dec 2 to 12 and the 10-day Kagyu Monlam Chenmo from Dec 13 to 22. The 2026-27 winter season of world peace pujas will conclude with the five-day third Thailand Chanting Ceremony from March 1 to 5.Anticipating a large influx of devotees and tourists, Union MSME minister Jitan Ram Manjhi and Bihar assembly Speaker Prem Kumar chaired a review meeting on Saturday evening. They directed district and police officials, along with representatives of hotel, travel and Buddhist organisations, to prepare a comprehensive plan to promote tourism and manage visitors.Following the meeting, district magistrate-cum-BTMC chairman Shashank Shubhankar asked officials to prepare a detailed traffic management plan for Bodh Gaya within four days. He directed them to identify separate parking zones for heavy vehicles, light vehicles and e-rickshaws, besides earmarking high-capacity parking areas.Reviewing the Mahavihara’s infrastructure, Shubhankar also directed officials to ensure uniform painting across the premises. articles.title: Odisha Khati Corner
articles.summary: Odisha Khati Corner: IAS officer typo “Angola” post goes viral; Subroto Bagchi highlights Odisha skills; BMC corporators protest garbage; IPS Bothra’s PR quip.
articles.body: Africa callingIAS officer Abdaal M Akhtar appears to have landed an overseas posting, at least on paper. An official letter meant for the collector and district magistrate of Angul, now spelt Anugola, addressed him instead as the collector and DM of “Angola”. Akhtar was quick to spot the rather ambitious typo and posted it on social media with a crisp update: “Transferred. Moving to Africa now.” A missing letter may usually invite a correction, but this one managed to move an IAS officer across continents.Skills on moveBusiness leader Subroto Bagchi may now be steering Karnataka’s newly constituted vision group for skill development, but Odisha’s skill story clearly continues to travel with him. Bagchi, who once headed Odisha Skill Development Authority, recently shared on social media his talk at Bangalore International Centre on Odisha’s “transformational work” in skill development. New platform, new role, different state, but when Bagchi talks skills, Odisha invariably finds its way into the presentation.Waste-side storyGarbage raised quite a stink at a recent BMC meeting, with corporators protesting over waste piling up in different parts of the city and demanding immediate action. As mayor Sulochana Das tried to address the uproar, the microphone reportedly malfunctioned, leaving her temporarily unheard amid an already noisy house. She later referred the matter to the BMC commissioner and assured corporators that the problem would be resolved within 10 days. One corporator, however, came armed with a Plan B — if the garbage wasn’t lifted, it would be dumped outside the BMC office. The warning drew laughter, though the civic body may not find the prospect quite as funny.Quick retortLaw and order apparently isn’t the only thing on senior IPS officer Arun Bothra’s radar. When an X user jokingly suggested he was doing PR for the Ambanis, the former journalist-turned-cop shot back with a line worthy of an ad pitch. “I don’t do PR for anyone. articles.title: Kareena Kapoor Khan steals the show in a Sabyasachi shirt, but her red accessories are the real stars
articles.summary: Kareena Kapoor Khan has this effortless way of making even the most basic pieces look like a million bucks.
articles.body: Kareena Kapoor Khan has this effortless way of making even the most basic pieces look like a million bucks. And her latest night out in Mumbai was proof of that. Attending the launch of The Library, the brand-new restaurant-cum-reading spot at NMACC, alongside her husband Saif Ali Khan, it was her surprisingly casual yet super-chic outfit that had everyone doing a double take.Instead of slipping into a traditional gown or an over-the-top festive outfit, Kareena pulled a fast one by reaching straight into the menswear section. She wore a printed silk shirt from Sabyasachi, tucked into tailored black trousers, and tied the whole thing together with a pop of bright red accessories. It wasn't loud or trying too hard, but it easily stole the show.Giving a Sabyasachi menswear shirt a whole new lifeThe centerpiece of Kareena’s look was easily that silk paisley shirt from Sabyasachi. Covered in a vintage-inspired print with muted tones of grey, dusty pink, and soft beige, it had a timeless, lived-in feel to it.Featuring a classic collar and a relaxed cut, she kept it from looking sloppy by tucking it neatly into high-waisted black trousers. To give the outfit some shape and a flash of contrast, she cinched her waist with a bold red belt featuring a heavy gold buckle. That single detail completely transformed the silhouette, giving the oversized shirt a sharp, tailored finish.Red accessories done rightKareena didn't shy away from playing with color. She doubled down on the red accents by carrying a iconic Bottega Veneta Knot clutch and stepping out in sky-high red Casadei Blade pumps.Matching your bag to your shoes used to be considered old-school, but here it worked like a charm. The vibrant red accessories pulled directly from the belt's tone, adding just the right amount of high-fashion drama without clashing against the shirt's detailed pattern. She kept her jewelry minimal, choosing subtle gold pieces from Sabyasachi that complemented the belt’s hardware.Soft glam that looks effortlessWhen it comes to hair and makeup, Kareena rarely misses. She stuck with her signature understated glam: clean, sculpted skin, defined brows, a touch of smudged kohl around her eyes, flushed cheeks, and a glossy nude-pink lip.Her dark hair was styled in long, loose waves with a deep side part, letting it fall naturally over her shoulders. It kept the whole vibe laid-back and cool, balancing out the high-end designer tags.Saif Ali Khan coordinates in tan and navySaif Ali Khan looked just as dapper standing beside her. He went for a relaxed tan suit paired with a navy blue dress shirt, leaving the top few buttons undone for an easygoing, suave look. A pair of retro yellow-tinted sunglasses and polished black dress shoes completed his outfit.The power couple was out to celebrate the grand opening of The Library, located inside Mumbai's Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC).What’s the buzz about the library at NMACC?Following a star-studded launch party on October 31, The Library officially opened its doors on November 1. It’s not just a quiet room with bookshelves - it’s a hybrid space designed to fuse literature, fine dining, and culture under a single roof.The venue boasts a curated collection of over 4,500 books sourced from top publishers globally. Visitors can spend hours flipping through titles spanning fiction, art, design, history, travel, and food, with options to buy whatever catches their eye.Nostalgia lovers are in for a treat, too. The space features the complete Amar Chitra Katha anthology, housed inside a dedicated 'Chariot of Wisdom' installation that showcases classic stories from Indian mythology, folklore, and history.On the culinary side, the menu was co-created by the NMACC team alongside famed restaurateur Aditi Dugar. The all-day dining spot offers everything from artisanal viennoiserie and fresh-baked breads to small plates, craft cocktails, hand-poured matcha, signature coffee blends, and gourmet chocolates.At the end of the day, Kareena’s outfit gave everyone a quick masterclass in personal style. You don't always need a heavy dress or complex layers to make an impression. articles.title: Western Himalaya’s Eurasian eagle-owl, one of the world’s largest owl species, photograped for the first time in Eastern Himalayan foothills near Buxa
articles.summary: First photo of a Eurasian eagle-owl spotted near Buxa Tiger Reserve in north Bengal, possibly the first record in eastern India, during a BWS-WWF owl survey.
articles.body: Kolkata: In what ornithologists are describing as a very unusual sighting, a Eurasian eagle-owl, one of the world’s largest owl species, has been photographed for the first time in the foothills of Eastern Himalayas, near Buxa Tiger Reserve in north Bengal. This could also be the first photographic record of the species from eastern India.Veteran birders Biswapriya Rahut and Samudra Sengupta photographed the bird on Saturday during an ongoing state-wide owl survey jointly conducted by the Birdwatchers’ Society (BWS) and WWF-India. Rahut is one of the founders of BWS.The Eurasian eagle-owl is primarily associated with the Western Himalayas, particularly Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh and adjoining high-altitude landscapes. It inhabits rocky, mountainous and semi-arid terrain, including parts of the Tibetan Plateau, where it has been recorded at elevations ranging from nearly 3,000 metres to over 4,500 metres.Ashwin Viswanathan, scientist and senior project manager at the Nature Conservation Foundation, said the species has also been recorded in Bhutan, which lies along the southern edge of the Tibetan Plateau. “But in eastern India, this is in all likelihood the first sighting and photographic record. Recent weather disturbances in Bhutan could have played a role in its appearance near Buxa,” Viswanathan said.The possibility of weather-related displacement is being explored as Buxa’s northern boundary runs along the Bhutan border. A glacial lake outburst flood at Shintaphu Lake in Bhutan’s Gasa on Oct 29 released around 7.4 million cubic metres of water into the Mo Chhu and Sankosh river systems. The flood wave travelled downstream towards north Bengal and lower Assam.Rahut pointed out that there was an earlier record of the species from Arunachal Pradesh. “In Nov 2006, ornithologist Rishad Naoroji recorded a calling pair at Larjup, between Chander and Tungri in Arunachal. It was documented as an isolated winter record,” he said.BWS founder Sujan Chatterjee said the ongoing survey, the first initiative of its kind in India, would help establish baseline data on owl species, their abundance and distribution across Bengal’s different habitats.
